narrative.overview:
Absent Aurora takes the character of a statistical publication in progress. The approved analysis editor is the visual reference: a navy working header, cool blue-gray canvas, and a white report surface. Clear controls support sustained analytical work while evidence and provenance remain visible.

Use this visual language across all views, including the dashboard, authentication, publications, series, events, and user workspace. New and revised screens should inherit its restrained typography, surface hierarchy, control shapes, spacing rhythm, and action hierarchy. Adapt composition to the task; the editor's guided configuration flow belongs to analysis creation and editing.

This is an app-wide design direction, not a completed migration of every screen. Outside the editor, light is the default and dark is an optional manual choice in the shared navigation. Never select a theme automatically from the system preference. Remember explicit choices across navigation and reloads when browser storage is available. Apply shared patterns through semantic DaisyUI roles in the active theme; palette or theme changes require a deliberate implementation in `src/styles/global.css`.
keyCharacteristics: Clear, contained controls with a distinct primary content surface.
Contained depth: structural separation with occasional elevation.
Functional color names that remain useful when palette values change.
Reusable components across views with explicit theme boundaries.

rules.name: Event correction provenance
rules.body: Correction provenance occupies a subdued region at the bottom of an event card: the immediate predecessor is labeled “Corrección de”, and an initially closed disclosure shows the number of direct corrections. Expanding it reveals their links, creation dates, and invalidity when applicable. These links clear the status filter and focus the linked event; URL fragments support direct access and a primary-colored ring highlights the target. The creation form identifies the event being corrected before submission. Correction relationships remain separate from validity badges.

rules.name: Event catalog composition
rules.body: The event catalog uses the analysis reader's bounded 1280px muted canvas. A visible heading and separate filter/action toolbar precede a grid of independent bordered event cards, with two columns from 1024px and one below. Cards have a subdued date strip with prominent day numerals and month/year; periods connect their start and end with an arrow, while single-date events are labeled “Hito puntual”. The title and expandable narrative lead the card body, followed by textual status and topic metadata. Geography and the external source link share a separated footer with small line icons. The compact, accessibly named actions menu leaves room for long titles. Cards size to their content and use active-theme surfaces and radii without hover elevation or nested cards. The inline creation form groups information, dates, and geography with fieldsets and thin rules; this form is also reused in the analysis editor. Catalog controls have 44px minimum heights and fields use 16px text below the desktop breakpoint. The catalog retains the active light or dark theme and its semantic colors; it does not apply the editor theme.

rules.name: The Theme Boundary Rule
rules.body: Carry the analysis view's visual hierarchy across all screens through semantic colors in the active theme. Keep literal editor palette values and editor-only tokens scoped until an explicit theme migration.

rules.name: The Shared Composition Rule
rules.body: Reuse the analysis view's bounded canvas, clear content surface, compact action group, and internal separators across routes. Preserve each view's task and information hierarchy rather than copying the editor's sidebar or steps.

rules.name: Analysis reader composition
rules.body: The analysis reader uses a single bordered report surface on a muted canvas, bounded to 1280px with responsive gutters. Its visible title, publication status, region, description, validity warnings, and linked versions precede a two-column indicator and period summary that stacks on mobile. Chart controls have 44px minimum targets; an accessible Help button toggles the initially hidden calendar and index-zero definitions; changes apply only to the current view. Source references use separated rows with explicit series links. Macro events and detailed values are expanded by default, with contained keyboard-focusable table scrolling, wrapped names, and right-aligned tabular values. The reader consumes the active light or dark theme and does not force the editor theme.

dos: Do reuse the existing component baseline before introducing another visual treatment.
Do use the approved analysis view as the visual reference for every new or revised screen.
Do adapt its surface, typography, control, and spacing patterns to each view's task.
Do name colors by their function and update this snapshot when their source values change.
Do preserve theme scope, including the editor's explicitly light theme.
Do prioritize usability, readable composition, and visible data provenance.
Do preserve Spanish labels and textual status explanations.
donts: Don't hard-code the editor palette into other views or bypass active-theme semantics.
Don't copy analysis-specific steps, hidden headings, or preview switching into unrelated views.
Don't introduce a separate rounded card around every report subsection.
Don't assume the bundled code font is the rendered font of every monospace utility.
Don't promote chart series colors or one-off utility values into brand tokens.
Don't claim browser verification from source inspection alone.
